articles.headline: Contract Year Dynamics Take Center Stage Across the Garage
articles.dek: A significant portion of the Cup Series grid enters the season with agreements expiring at the conclusion of 2026.
articles.body:
As the 2026 season gets underway at Daytona International Speedway, attention extends beyond the racing surface to the business side of the garage. Several prominent drivers begin the year operating in the final season of their current agreements, establishing a unique dynamic for team leadership and driver management.

Team Penske features multiple drivers in contract years, including Ryan Blaney and Austin Cindric. Both drivers enter the season content with their current positions as they evaluate the competitive landscape. Over at Hendrick Motorsports, Kyle Larson also races through the final year of his deal, maintaining a steady approach as championship preparations finalize.

RFK Racing carries significant contract-year representation with Chris Buescher. Team management has emphasized stability across the organization as they build on previous momentum. In the 23XI Racing camp, Tyler Reddick enters the final year of his agreement while teammate Bubba Wallace remains secured through 2027.

Additional names navigating final-year deals include Wood Brothers Racing driver Josh Berry and Trackhouse Racing competitor Shane Van Gisbergen. While silly season speculation typically accelerates later in the summer, the early months provide drivers an opportunity to establish performance baselines before negotiations begin in earnest.

Front office personnel have noted that contract statuses rarely impact on-track execution during the initial races, but consistent results remain paramount for secure futures across the paddock.
articles.author: Cole Whitaker

pullQuote.text: Our focus right now is entirely on winning races and starting the year strong.

articles.headline: Hamlin Leads Daytona Preseason Test Speed Charts
articles.dek: Joe Gibbs Racing driver paces the field as teams complete final preparations for the Daytona 500.
articles.body:
Denny Hamlin established the benchmark during the single-car and drafting runs at Daytona International Speedway, turning the fastest lap in the #11 Joe Gibbs Racing Toyota. Hamlin's quick lap set the pace for a competitive garage area as teams worked through various aerodynamic and drafting programs ahead of the season opener.

Chase Briscoe slotted into second place in his first official appearance with Joe Gibbs Racing, validating the speed of his equipment during the multi-car drafting sessions. Ryan Preece put RFK Racing third on the speed chart, followed by Team Penske driver Ryan Blaney in fourth and 23XI Racing's Tyler Reddick in fifth.

Christopher Bell rounded out the top six for Joe Gibbs Racing, while Kyle Larson led the Hendrick Motorsports contingent in seventh place. Chase Elliott and William Byron placed eighth and ninth, giving Hendrick three cars inside the top ten. Bubba Wallace completed the top ten for 23XI Racing.

Garage observers noted that test speeds at superspeedways rarely tell the full story, as teams frequently employ different engine configurations and drag packages to evaluate handling rather than raw speed. Drafting lines formed throughout the afternoon as drivers practiced pushing and lane management in preparation for Sunday's race.

Teams will now transition from testing mode to official practice and qualifying sessions. The 2026 Daytona 500 is scheduled for February 15 at Daytona International Speedway.
articles.author: Ross Delgado

articles.headline: Evaluating the Roster Landscape Before the Season Opener
articles.dek: A comprehensive look at the championship favorites, dark horses, and new combinations heading into the season.
articles.body:
The 2026 Virtual NASCAR Cup Series season brings a familiar set of powerhouse organizations to the front of the grid, led by Joe Gibbs Racing and Hendrick Motorsports. Denny Hamlin topped the speed charts in the preseason test at Daytona International Speedway with a lap of the 2.5-mile superspeedway, signaling that the veteran driver and his Joe Gibbs Racing team are ready to contend immediately. Chase Briscoe settled into the second spot during testing in his new tenure with Joe Gibbs Racing, proving that the transition to the organization has been smooth.

RFK Racing showed formidable single-lap speed during the testing sessions. Ryan Preece placed third in the #60 machine, while teammate Chris Buescher landed sixteenth. Preece enters the year looking to maximize his opportunities in top-tier equipment, while Buescher works alongside Brad Keselowski to push RFK further up the manufacturer standings.

Hendrick Motorsports maintains a potent lineup consisting of Kyle Larson, Chase Elliott, William Byron, and Alex Bowman. Larson posted the seventh-fastest time in testing. Elliott and Byron followed closely in eighth and ninth respectively, establishing a solid baseline for the Chevrolet camp.

Further down the sheet, 23XI Racing showed promise with Tyler Reddick taking fifth and Bubba Wallace tenth. Team Penske utilized a conservative testing program, with Ryan Blaney fourth, Joey Logano twelfth, and Austin Cindric seventeenth. With the Daytona 500 looming, teams have finalized their setups and are preparing for 500 miles of restrictor-plate racing.
articles.author: Wes Ostrander
